summary: Hold by this hypothesis's own condition ('worth running only once stage 3 shows A8 at or near its gate'). Stage 3's wgmma kernel failed its self-check (case 2, rel L2 1.23 for ticket and B8) and never ran, so there is no gate evidence. Batch-1 full verify at grid = SM count puts about 9.5 tiles in each CTA, which is exactly the multi-tile regime that failed, so this run would fall back to master FA3 and measure nothing. Fix stage 3 first, then re-mint.
justification: Parent facts (archive/full-verify-wgmma-s3-warpgroup-per-kvhead-inproc/2c3f7fff72bb4e1d.log). Build and occupancy were good: 128 regs, 0 local, sm_90a, 2 CTAs/SM. The canary and case 1 passed, but in both every CTA had at most 1 tile (3 tiles over grid 4; 242 tiles over grid 264). Case 2 (lens_a, kv_scale 0.25, grid 3, about 81 tiles per CTA) failed at rel L2 1.23 in both ticket and B8 modes, so the fault is in the main kernel's multi-tile machinery (ring and mbarrier phase wrap, V^T double-buffer reuse, Q reload across requests, page-index rotation past 16 tiles), or else in kv_scale handling; the two are confounded. Fallback: 'full verify master FA3, paired heads'. The 1.380x is master re-measured: verify_16/32 at 162.61/301.91 us equal the incumbent's 162.7/301.3. This hypothesis's speed estimate rests on 'the stage-3 gate rate (>= 2.4 TB/s)', which was never measured; the only measured CUDA verify rate is stage 2's A8 at 1.44 TB/s. At batch 1 with 80000 keys (1250 tiles) and grid 132, each CTA runs about 9.5 tiles, and the specified self-check (80000/4097 keys, grids 3/7/SM) will hit the failing regime. Request crossing cannot occur at batch 1, so this would be a partial bisect if the bug is request crossing; it would still fail if the bug is ring phase, V^T reuse or kv_scale. The design itself is sound on its merits. Full verify_1 is 30.0 us (FA3 main 15.0 + combine 7.6 + prepare 2.7) against a 4.3 us floor, weight 16, and FINDINGS confirms it. One launch at grid = SM count, with a two-level ticket merge replacing a single-CTA 4.3 MB merge, is the right shape. sqrt-grouping (about 12 groups of 11) brings the serial merge down to about 11 x 32 KB per level. WEAKEST LINK (after the fix): 20.5 MB in about 8.5 us needs 2.4 TB/s from one request on 132 CTAs at 1 CTA/SM. That is half the resident CTAs the kernel was tuned for (2 per SM), so the bytes in flight per SM halve. A 4-stage ring of 16 KB tiles gives about 64 KB per SM, which is marginal for 2.4 TB/s at around 1 us of latency. grid = 2 x SM, with 4.7 tiles per CTA, may be faster at batch 1. Make the grid a prepare-time sweep (SM, 2 x SM) rather than fixing SM count.
confounders: full-verify-wgmma-s3-warpgroup-per-kvhead-inproc (parent): it fell back, so the 'stage-3 kernel' this widens has no timing and fails correctness in the regime batch 1 needs.

paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: master runs full verify batch 1 UNPAIRED (paired requires batch > 1), so widening the gate to batch 1 keeps the q layout. On fallback, batch 1 must stay on master's unpaired FA3 path (as the spec says), not on a paired one.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv / full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (not landed): the same two-level ticket idea for decode batch 1 reached 1.432x without promotion. Reusing its group-ticket code is fine, but its buffers must be separate per module.
interference: No companion: the result is read from the replaced kernel's own profile row, and the obstacle is that the run would measure the fallback, which no A/B fixes. The prerequisite is a stage-3 correctness fix (the same one proposed for the sibling full-verify-wgmma-s4-sliding-window). Its self-check bisects case 2: (lens_a, 1.0, grid 3) vs (lens_a, 0.25, grid 264); a single request at N = 2, 4 and 17 tiles per CTA; and the device error word printed. Once that passes and full verify_16/32 show the kernel's own time, re-mint this unchanged, with the grid as a prepare-time sweep of {SM, 2 x SM} at batch 1.
rules_flags: None blocking. The gate is config-only (batch from cfg), the grid choice is shape-only, the group-ticket buffer is a zero int32 buffer from import that is reset in-kernel, and every key of the 80000 is covered by the stream-K tiles.
Two replays in the self-check must verify that BOTH ticket levels reset to 0. A stale group ticket would silently skip a merge in the timed graph replays.
open_questions: Is the stage-3 failure from multiple tiles per CTA or from kv_scale 0.25? A batch-1 run only exercises the first, without request crossing.
At batch 1, does grid = SM count (1 CTA/SM, about 64 KB in flight per SM) actually beat 2 x SM? Sweep both in prepare().
What does the two-level merge's tail actually cost? Stamp it with clock64 in the self-check; the spec's ~2 us is an estimate.
